title: Service-identity permission must cover the target plugin route's ACL
answers: Why does a service-identity background job get 403/forbidden calling a plugin route through the datasource proxy?
ExternalAMSyncer/ruler syncer fetch fails with access denied even though it uses the service identity
What permission do I need to add when a new sync worker proxies to a new datasource/plugin endpoint?
body: Symptom: a background worker using identity.WithServiceIdentity to call a datasource/plugin route through the proxy gets rejected by the route's own RBAC check. Root cause: serviceIdentityPermissions (pkg/apimachinery/identity/context.go) is a fixed wildcard permission list; it must explicitly include the accesscontrol action the target plugin route enforces (e.g. alert.notifications.external:read, required by the Alertmanager plugin's GET api/v1/alerts route used by ExternalAMSyncer). Fix pattern: when wiring a new proxied request type for a service-identity caller, add the specific route's required action to serviceIdentityPermissions with a comment naming the route and consumer. Constraints: only needed for routes/plugins that enforce RBAC; irrelevant for unauthenticated or unchecked endpoints.
applies: Any new background/service-identity call that is routed through a plugin or datasource proxy endpoint guarded by RBAC.
says: Background worker gets 403 forbidden calling plugin route through the proxy.
Service identity denied access to datasource endpoint via proxy request.
Syncer fails with access denied even though it uses service identity.
Missing permission for service identity to access plugin route.
What permission do I add when a sync worker proxies to plugin endpoint?
search: Background workers using identity.WithServiceIdentity to call datasource or plugin routes through the proxy must have the target route's required RBAC action explicitly added to serviceIdentityPermissions in pkg/apimachinery/identity/context.go with a comment naming the route and consumer (e.g. alert.notifications.external:read for ExternalAMSyncer calling Alertmanager plugin's GET api/v1/alerts). Without the matching permission, the service identity gets rejected by the route's own RBAC check. Constraint: only required for routes/plugins that enforce RBAC; irrelevant for unauthenticated or unchecked endpoints. Applies to any new proxied request type initiated by a service-identity background caller.
